claim: SARS-CoV-2 has infected millions of individuals and resulted in >4 million deaths.
source: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the virus that causes coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), has infected millions of individuals, resulted in >4 million deaths, and greatly disrupted societies worldwide (Dong et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dong et al., 2020

claim: Recovered individuals mostly exhibit robust humoral and cellular SARS-CoV-2 immunity.
source: Recovered individuals mostly exhibit robust humoral and cellular SARS-CoV-2 immunity (Grifoni et al., 2020; Koutsakos et al., 2021; Mathew et al., 2020; Sekine et al., 2020; Thevarajan et al., 2020) and generate immunological memory.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: The mRNA vaccines BNT162b2 and mRNA-1273 successfully induce SARS-CoV-2-specific humoral immunity.
source: Several studies in healthy individuals demonstrated that the mRNA vaccines, BNT162b2 (Pfizer-BioNTech) and mRNA-1273 (Moderna), successfully induce SARS-CoV-2-specific humoral (Gaebler et al., 2021; Ma et al., 2020) and cellular immunity (Collier et al., 2021; Minervina et al., 2021; Oberhardt et al., 2021; Sahin et al., 2021)
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: The mRNA vaccines are highly efficacious (>94%) in reducing transmissibility and induction of serious disease and hospitalization.
source: are highly efficacious (>94%) in reducing transmissibility and induction of serious disease and hospitalization of most variants (Baden et al., 2021; Lyngse et al., 2021; Polack et al., 2020; Tenforde and Patel, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: About 4% of the world's population is affected by one of over 80 different types of autoimmune disease.
source: However, about 4% of the world's population is affected by one of over 80 different types of autoimmune disease, including common conditions such as multiple sclerosis (MS) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) (National Stem Cell Foundation, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to National Stem Cell Foundation, 2021

claim: The severity of COVID-19 in individuals on immunosuppressants varies from mild to severe, depending on the type of immunosuppressants.
source: The severity of COVID-19 in individuals on immunosuppressants varies from mild to severe, depending on the type of immunosuppressants (Gianfrancesco et al., 2020; Möhn et al., 2020; Sparks et al., 2021; Strangfeld et al., 2021) and other underlying risk factors (Baden et al., 2021; Chaudhry et al., 2021; Hughes et al., 2021; Möhn et al., 2020; Pablos et al., 2020; Sparks et al., 2021; Strangfeld et al., 2021; Williamson et al., 2020; Zabalza et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published studies

claim: A single dose of mRNA vaccine in SARS-CoV-2 experienced healthy individuals resulted in stronger and broader immune responses than with vaccination alone.
source: Recent studies demonstrated that a single dose of mRNA vaccine in SARS-CoV-2 experienced healthy individuals resulted in stronger and broader immune responses than with vaccination alone, the so-called hybrid immunity (Reynolds et al., 2021; Stamatatos et al., 2021; Tauzin et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2021a).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: The majority of patients on anti-CD20 therapies did not generate significant SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody titers following natural infection.
source: However, the majority of patients on anti-CD20 therapies did not generate significant SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody titers following the natural infection (Koutsakos et al., 2021; Simon et al., 2021; Zabalza et al., 2021) or vaccination (Apostolidis et al., 2021; Deepak et al., 2021; van Kempen et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: Low vaccination-induced SARS-CoV-2 antibody titers in anti-CD20-treated MS patients correlate with reduced frequencies of circulating B cells and low Tfh cells.
source: A study in SARS-CoV-2 naïve anti-CD20-treated MS patients demonstrated that low vaccination-induced SARS-CoV-2 antibody titers correlate with reduced frequencies of circulating B cells (in line with anti-CD20-mediated B cell depletion) and low Tfh cells (Apostolidis et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Apostolidis et al., 2021

claim: SARS-CoV-2 naïve anti-CD20-treated MS patients which induced the lowest antibody titers displayed the highest induction of activated CD8+ T cells after vaccination.
source: Interestingly, SARS-CoV-2 naïve anti-CD20-treated MS patients which induced the lowest antibody titers displayed the highest induction of activated CD8+ T cells after vaccination (Apostolidis et al., 2021; Brill et al., 2021; Gadani et al., 2021; Madelon et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: CD8+ T cells are essential for viral clearance.
source: CD8+ T cells form an important second line of protection against severe illness and mortality, as they are essential for the viral clearance (Kundu et al., 2022; Tan et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kundu et al., 2022 and Tan et al., 2021

claim: MTX has been reported to reduce antibody titers after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in SARS-CoV-2 naïve autoimmune patients.
source: it has also been reported to reduce antibody titers after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in SARS-CoV-2 naïve autoimmune patients (Deepak et al., 2021; Furer et al., 2021; Haberman et al., 2020; Spiera et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: mRNA vaccination of SARS-CoV-2 naïve MTX-treated patients with IMID did not induce activated CD8+ T cells.
source: In contrast to anti-CD20-treated MS patients, mRNA vaccination of SARS-CoV-2 naïve MTX-treated patients with immune-mediated inflammatory disease (IMID) did not induce activated CD8+ T cells following mRNA vaccination (Haberman et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Haberman et al., 2020

claim: The cohort consisted of 7 OCR-treated relapsing-remitting MS patients, 6 MTX-treated RA patients, and 15 healthy controls.
source: The cohort consisted of 7 OCR-treated relapsing-remitting MS (MS-OCR) patients, 6 MTX-treated RA patients (RA-MTX), and 15 HCs (Figure 1a and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Direct statement about study cohort composition

claim: The median age, sex, and time since SARS-CoV-2 infection were comparable between all three groups.
source: The median age, sex, and time since SARS-CoV-2 infection (Figure 1b) were comparable between all three groups, although the RA-MTX group had a slightly higher prevalence of comorbidities (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Direct statement about demographic comparability with reference to data

claim: Patients received their first mRNA-1273 vaccination on average 210 (71–490) days post infection.
source: Patients received their first mRNA-1273 (Moderna) vaccination after full recovery from their SARS-CoV-2 infection, on average 210 (71–490) days post infection.
evidence: Direct statement with specific numerical data

claim: OCR treatment is known to eliminate CD20+ B cell populations for prolonged periods.
source: OCR treatment is known to eliminate CD20+ B cell populations for prolonged periods (van Lierop et al., 2022)
evidence: Supported by citation to van Lierop et al., 2022

claim: Based on IgG titers, the majority of SARS-CoV-2 experienced RA-MTX (67%), MS-OCR patients (50%), and HC (58%) still had detectible antibody titers before vaccination.
source: Based on IgG titers, the majority of SARS-CoV-2 experienced RA-MTX (67%), MS-OCR patients (50%), and HC (58%) still had detectible antibody titers (antibody titers above the cutoff of 4 AU/ml levels; determined using 600 pre-COVID-19 outbreak samples as published before) (Steenhuis et al., 2021; Vogelzang et al., 2020; Figure 2a and Figure 2—figure supplement 1a, b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures and citations to published methods

claim: 100% of RA-MTX patients and HCs seroconverted for IgG following the first vaccination.
source: Vaccine-induced humoral recall responses were observed in SARS-CoV-2 experienced RA-MTX patients and HCs as 100% of the individuals seroconverted for IgG following the first vaccination (T1) and was maintained for the duration of the study ( Figure 4-figure supplement 1 b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure supplement

claim: RA-MTX patients displayed significantly lower RBD IgG levels at day 7 post first vaccination compared to HC.
source: Although RA-MTX patients displayed a slight increase in RBD IgG levels at day 7 post first vaccination (T1) (Figure 2a), they were significantly lower as compared to HC (Figure 2b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2a and 2b

claim: By day 42 post first vaccination, RA-MTX IgG levels had significantly increased to levels comparable to those observed in vaccinated HCs.
source: While by day 42 post first vaccination (T2), RA-MTX IgG levels had significantly increased to levels comparable to those observed in vaccinated HCs and a similar trend was observed for IgA and IgM (Figure 2a–b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2a-b

claim: No changes in antibody titers following both vaccinations were observed in SARS-CoV-2 experienced MS-OCR patients.
source: No changes in antibody titers following both vaccinations were observed in SARS-CoV-2 experienced MS-OCR patients (Figure 2a and Figure 2—figure supplement 1b)
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: The combination of all three isotypes specific for RBD was not detected in any of the vaccinated SARS-CoV-2 experienced MS-OCR patients.
source: Most notably, the combination of all three isotypes specific for RBD was not detected in any of the vaccinated SARS-CoV-2 experienced MS-OCR patients neither before nor after both vaccinations (Figure 2c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2c

claim: B cells were almost absent in MS-OCR patients.
source: While HC showed an expected increase in the number and proportion of total B cells at 7 days post first vaccination (T1), this was not observed in RA-MTX patients and B cells were almost absent in MS-OCR patients, in line with the B cell-depleting function of OCR (Figure 2d).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2d and known mechanism of OCR

claim: A significantly lower number of memory B cells was observed in SARS-CoV-2 experienced MS-OCR and RA-MTX patients compared to HCs at all three time points.
source: including a significantly lower number of memory B cells in SARS-CoV-2 experienced MS-OCR and RA-MTX patients compared to HCs at all three time points (T0, T1, and T3) (Figure 2f and Figure 2—figure supplement 1c, d).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: No increase in plasmablasts and plasma cells were observed in the majority of SARS-CoV-2 experienced RA-MTX and MS-OCR patients upon vaccination.
source: Interestingly, although two RA-MTX patients and one MS-OCR patient displayed an increase in plasmablast and plasma cell numbers and proportions (Figure 2g–h and Figure 2—figure supplement 1d), no increase in plasmablasts and plasma cells were observed in the majority of the SARS-CoV-2 experienced RA-MTX and MS-OCR patients upon vaccination (Figure 2g–h).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: A significantly higher number and proportion of plasmablast and plasma cells were observed following the first but not second vaccination of SARS-CoV-2 experienced HCs.
source: A significantly higher number and proportion of plasmablast and plasma cells were observed following the first but not second vaccination of SARS-CoV-2 experienced HCs (Figure 2g–h and Figure 2—figure supplement 1d)
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: A significantly smaller Tfh1 cell population was observed in RA-MTX and MS-OCR patients compared to HC before vaccination.
source: While the number and proportion of most CD4+ cTfh subsets were remarkably similar between HC and both patients groups, a significantly smaller Tfh1 cell population was observed in RA-MTX and MS-OCR patients as compared to HC before vaccination (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a, b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure supplement

claim: A significant increase in the number of CD4+ cTfh1, cTfhTripPos, and cTfhTripNeg cells was determined upon first vaccination in HC, whereas this population remained unchanged in the patient groups.
source: Interestingly, a significant increase in the number of CD4+ cTfh1, cTfhTripPos, and cTfhTripNeg cells was determined upon first vaccination in HC, whereas this population remained unchanged in the patient groups (Figure 3c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3c

claim: The CD4+ cTfh1, cTfh17, and cTfhTripPos subsets are the most responsive after the first vaccination.
source: Analysis of the proportion of responding cells (cells that upregulated one or more dynamic markers) demonstrated that the CD4+ cTfh1, cTfh17, and cTfhTripPos subsets are the most responsive after the first vaccination (Figure 3e and Figure 3—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: MS-OCR patients showed a slightly higher combined expression of three dynamic markers on CD4+ cTfh1 cells following first vaccination compared to HCs.
source: A slightly higher combined expression of three dynamic markers on CD4+ cTfh1 cells following first vaccination was observed in MS-OCR patients compared to HCs, whereas the combined expression of multiple dynamic markers in RA-MTX patients was slightly lower compared to HCs (Figure 3f and Figure 3—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: Vaccination promoted the expansion of the Th1 cell population in HC only.
source: Although the size of the Th1 population was comparable between HC and the patient groups, vaccination did promote the expansion of the Th1 cell population in HC only, which resulted in significantly more Th1 cells in HC after two vaccinations as compared to the patient groups (Figure 4c–d and Figure 4—figure supplement 1a, b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: After the first vaccination the size of Th1-like cell population was significantly higher in HC.
source: Furthermore, vaccination did not affect the size of the Th1-like population in the individual groups, however, after the first vaccination the size Th1-like cell population was significantly higher in HC where it only tended to be higher before vaccination (Figure 4e–f and Figure 4—figure supplement 1a, b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: A profound increase in responding CD4+ Th1 cells was observed in all SARS-CoV-2 experienced groups after the first vaccination, which was significant for the HC.
source: A profound increase in responding CD4+ Th1 cells was observed in all SARS-CoV-2 experienced groups after the first vaccination, which was significant for the HC (Figure 4h).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4h

claim: A greater proportion of CD4+ Th1 and Th1-like responding cells in MS-OCR patients co-expressed three dynamic markers compared to HCs.
source: Nevertheless, a greater proportion of CD4+ Th1 and Th1-like responding cells in MS-OCR patients co-expressed three dynamic markers compared to HCs (Figure 4j–k, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: A significantly lower total CD8+ T cell number per µl blood was observed in RA-MTX patients compared to HCs.
source: No significant changes in total CD8+ T cells numbers per µl blood were observed in MTX-RA, MS-OCR, and HCs after the first and second vaccination (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a), however, a significantly lower total CD8+ T cell number per µl blood was observed in RA-MTX patients compared to HCs (Figure 5b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: The smaller total CD8+ T cell population in RA-MTX patients was mainly driven by fewer CD8+ Tnaïve cells compared to HCs.
source: The smaller total CD8+ T cell population in RA-MTX patients was mainly driven by fewer CD8+ Tnaïve cells compared to HCs throughout the duration of the study (Figure 5c and Figure 5—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: MS-OCR patients display a substantial increase in CD8+ Tcm cell count per µl blood and proportions after the first vaccination.
source: Nevertheless, MS-OCR patients display a substantial increase in CD8+ Tcm cell count per µl blood and proportions after the first vaccination (Figure 5—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure supplement

claim: In RA-MTX patients, a significantly higher proportion of CD8+ Tcm cells expressed CD38 after the first vaccination.
source: In RA-MTX patients, a significantly higher proportion of CD8+ Tcm cells expressed CD38 after the first vaccination, whereas a more dynamic recall response was observed after the second vaccination where a greater proportion of CD8+ Tcm cells exhibited expression of CD38, PD1, TIGIT, and CD40L (Figure 5d and Figure 5—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: A higher proportion of CD8+ Tcm cells in MS-OCR patients displayed expression of CD38, HLA-DR, and TIGIT after the first vaccination.
source: In contrast, a higher proportion of CD8+ Tcm cells in MS-OCR patients displayed expression of CD38, HLA-DR, and TIGIT already after the first vaccination (Figure 5d).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 5d

claim: A profound increase in the percentage of responding CD8+ Tcm cells was observed in MS-OCR patients after the first vaccination.
source: In addition, a profound increase in the percentage of responding CD8+ Tcm cells was observed in MS-OCR patients after the first vaccination, of which substantially more cells co-expressed three to four dynamic markers following first vaccination compared to HCs (Figure 5f and Figure 5—figure supplement 1e)
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: RA-MTX patients displayed a vast increase in the percentage of responding CD8+ Tnaïve-like cells after the second vaccination.
source: RA-MTX patients displayed a vast increase in the percentage of responding CD8+ Tnaïve-like cells after the second vaccination, whereas MS-OCR patients displayed an increase in the percentage of responding CD8+ Tnaïve-like cells after the first vaccination which remained higher after the second vaccination (Figure 5e).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 5e

claim: OCR-treated MS patients exhibit a preserved recall response of CD8+ T central memory cells following first vaccination compared to HCs.
source: OCR-treated MS patients exhibit a preserved recall response of CD8+ T central memory cells following first vaccination compared to HCs and a similar CD4+ circulating T follicular helper 1 and T helper 1 dynamics, whereas humoral and B cell responses were strongly impaired resulting in absence of SARS-CoV-2-specific humoral immunity.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the abstract supported by data presented throughout the manuscript

claim: MTX treatment significantly delayed antibody levels and B reactivation following the first vaccination.
source: MTX treatment significantly delayed antibody levels and B reactivation following the first vaccination, including sustained inhibition of overall reactivation marker dynamics of the responding CD4+ and CD8+ T cells.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the abstract supported by data presented throughout the manuscript

claim: SARS-CoV-2 experienced MS-OCR patients may still benefit from vaccination by inducing a broad CD8+ T cell response which has been associated with milder disease outcome.
source: Together, these findings indicate that SARS-CoV-2 experienced MS-OCR patients may still benefit from vaccination by inducing a broad CD8+ T cell response which has been associated with milder disease outcome.
evidence: This is an inference based on the study findings and cited literature on CD8+ T cell responses

claim: The delayed vaccine-induced IgG kinetics in RA-MTX patients indicate an increased risk after the first vaccination.
source: The delayed vaccine-induced IgG kinetics in RA-MTX patients indicate an increased risk after the first vaccination, which might require additional shielding or alternative strategies such as treatment interruptions in vulnerable patients.
evidence: This is an inference based on the study findings about delayed antibody responses

claim: MTX has broad immunomodulating functions affecting multiple arms of the immune system.
source: MTX has broad immunomodulating functions affecting multiple arms of the immune system and has been shown to reduce circulating leukocytes numbers (neutrophils and lymphocytes), their proliferation capacity, T cell receptor (TCR) activation, T cell lytic capacity, inhibiting pro-inflammatory pathways, neutrophil recruitment, extracellular trap formation and cytokine expression by macrophages and increasing the number of regulatory T cells (Tregs) (Cronstein and Aune, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cronstein and Aune, 2020

claim: B cells play a critical role in the formation of protective humoral immunity during viral infections.
source: However, B cells play a critical role in the formation of protective humoral immunity during viral infections.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about B cell function

claim: With help from cognate CD4+ T follicular helper cells, B cells differentiate into memory B cells and plasmablasts or long-lived plasma cells that secrete class-switched, high-affinity antibodies.
source: With help from cognate CD4+ T follicular helper cells (Tfh cells), B cells differentiate into memory B cells and plasmablasts or long-lived plasma cells that secrete class-switched, high-affinity antibodies upon antigen stimulation through infection or vaccination (Elsner and Shlomchik, 2020; Nutt et al., 2015; Verstegen et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: Both B and Tfh cells are of great importance for the formation of protective humoral immunity in SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: SARS-CoV-2 infection in otherwise healthy individuals has demonstrated that both B and Tfh cells are of great importance for the formation of a protective humoral immunity (Koutsakos et al., 2021; Mathew et al., 2020; Ng et al., 2020; Thevarajan et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2021b).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: Tfh cells play a critical role in helping B cell activation and differentiation, antibody production, class switching, and somatic hypermutations.
source: Tfh cells play a critical role in helping B cell activation and differentiation, antibody production, class switching, and somatic hypermutations which further strengthen overall antibody responses upon infection and vaccination (Figure 1e; Koutsakos et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Koutsakos et al., 2019 and established knowledge

claim: Robust CD8+ T cell immunity has been shown to result in overall milder symptoms in SARS-CoV-2 patients.
source: Although CD8+ T cells do not prevent infection, they have a key role in viral clearance which contributes to the resolution of symptoms (Kundu et al., 2022; Thevarajan et al., 2020) and robust CD8+ T cell immunity has been shown to result in overall milder symptoms in SARS-CoV-2 patients (Rydyznski Moderbacher et al., 2020; Tan et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: CD8+ T cells recognize conserved epitopes allowing for high cross-reactivity between different SARS-CoV-2 variants.
source: Furthermore, CD8+ T cells recognize conserved epitopes allowing for high cross-reactivity between different SARS-CoV-2 variants (Alison Tarke et al., 2021; Gao et al., 2022; GeurtsvanKessel et al., 2021; Keeton et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2022; Rowntree et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple published studies

claim: High proportions of CD8+ T cells have been associated with clinically favorable outcomes.
source: While CD8+ T cells immunity will not prevent infection, high proportions of CD8+ T cells have been associated with clinically favorable outcomes (Kundu et al., 2022; Tan et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies

claim: The study was approved by the medical ethical committee and registered at Dutch Trial Register.
source: This study was approved by the medical ethical committee (NL74974.018.20 and EudraCT 2021-001102-30, local METC number: 2020_194) and registered at Dutch Trial Register (Trial ID NL8900).
evidence: Direct statement about study approval and registration

claim: Participants were vaccinated between April 19, 2021, and July 1, 2021, with the mRNA-1273 (Moderna) vaccine at an interval of six weeks.
source: Participants were recruited between April 16, 2021, and May 20, 2021, at the MS Center Amsterdam, Amsterdam UMC, and the Amsterdam READE Rheumatology and Immunology Center and vaccinated between April 19, 2021, and July 1, 2021, with the mRNA-1273 (Moderna) vaccine at an interval of six weeks, according to the Dutch national vaccination guidelines.
evidence: Direct statement about vaccination timing and protocol

claim: Fresh whole blood was used to measure cellular immune populations using two human antibody panels.
source: Fresh whole blood was used to measure cellular immune populations, essentially as described in Koutsakos et al., 2021; Thevarajan et al., 2020, using two human antibody panels (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Direct statement about methodology with citations

claim: In total 38 unique flow cytometry markers were combined with a computational pipeline in the Spectre R package.
source: In total 38 unique flow cytometry markers (Supplementary file 2) were combined with a computational pipeline in the Spectre R package (Ashhurst et al., 2021), encompassing the rPCA (from Seurat) (Hao et al., 2021), FlowSOM (Van Gassen et al., 2015), and Flt-SNE (fast Fourier transform-accelerated interpolation-based t-stochastic neighborhood embedding) (Linderman et al., 2019) algorithms
evidence: Direct statement about methodology with citations

claim: 42 different cell populations were identified by the computational analysis.
source: resulting in the identification of clusters representing major myeloid, innate, and lymphocyte lineages and their phenotype and activation status (Figure 1d–e and Figure 1—figure supplement 1a, b). In total, 42 different cell populations were identified
evidence: Direct statement about analysis results with reference to figures

claim: Circulating plasmablast and plasma cells could still be observed in MS-OCR patients in line with the absence of CD20 expression in these cell types.
source: Interestingly, circulating plasmablast and plasma cells could still be observed in line with the absence of CD20 expression in these cell types (Figure 1d).
evidence: Observation from data with mechanistic explanation based on known biology

claim: The number of non-classical monocytes per μl blood was significantly reduced in RA-MTX following both first and second vaccination.
source: The number of non-classical monocytes per μl blood was significantly reduced in RA-MTX following the both first and second vaccination, whereas in HC and MS-OCR a substantial reduction was observed (Figure 1g and Figure 1—figure supplement 3a-c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: The number of neutrophils and classical monocytes per μl blood were significantly reduced in HCs following the first vaccination.
source: In addition, the number of neutrophils and classical monocytes per μl blood were significantly reduced in HCs following the first vaccination (Figure 1g and Figure 1—figure supplement 3a-c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figures

claim: An increased expression of the activation marker CD38 was observed on a broad range of NK subsets in all groups following both vaccinations.
source: In contrast, an increased expression of the activation marker CD38 was observed on a broad range of NK subsets in all groups following both vaccinations as compared to the baseline sample (Figure 1—figure supplement 3d).
evidence: Supported by data shown in figure supplement

claim: MTX is known to hamper the proliferation of lymphocytes.
source: MTX is known to hamper the proliferation of lymphocytes (Cronstein and Aune, 2020)
evidence: Supported by citation to Cronstein and Aune, 2020

claim: OCR treatment mainly eradicated circulating CD20+ B cell populations, while B cells in secondary lymphoid organs may have been less affected.
source: One possibility is that OCR treatment mainly eradicated circulating CD20+ B cell populations, while B cells in secondary lymphoid organs may have been less affected (Kamburova et al., 2013).
evidence: This is speculation based on citation to Kamburova et al., 2013
